html:
SMTO-SKL-0035 — SMTO doesn't have permission for this Drive file yet

GUID: c807ea0e-390b-5f2f-b261-cfa96ef3a315
Slug: google-drive-scope-missing
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-drive

What happened

  • Your Google account hasn't given SMTO the kind of Drive access this needs. By default SMTO only sees files it created or that you opened with it, and permission to read does not include permission to change.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Decide what SMTO needs: to see or read your other Drive files, or also to change them. Google keeps reading and changing as separate permissions, and SMTO asks only for what you approve.
  2. Ask SMTO to reconnect your Google account with that access, for example "Reconnect my Google account so you can read all my Drive files." Your current approval only covers files SMTO created or that you opened with it.
  3. Open the Google sign-in link, choose the same Google account as before, and allow the new access. Using the same account adds the access to the existing connection instead of creating a second one.

What success looks like

  • SMTO can open the file and finish the request without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't approve access to everything if you only need SMTO to read files.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Drive access was refused for missing OAuth scope: Google returned insufficient scopes, the local feature check rejected the grant, or file-mode visibility rejected a file that is not app-authorized.

What this means

  • Google reports insufficient OAuth scope, local feature checks reject the grant, or file-mode visibility rejects an app-unauthorized file. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Google reports insufficient OAuth scope, local feature checks reject the grant, or file-mode visibility rejects an app-unauthorized file.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish missing OAuth feature from file-mode app authorization and broader all-mode intent.

How to fix it

  • In access_mode "file", DriveService._info rejects files where isAppAuthorized is false; Google insufficientPermissions/insufficientAuthenticationScopes and local scope_upgrade_required also map here. Only with the user's intent, use access_mode "all" and reconnect the same account key requesting drive_metadata_read, drive_read_all or drive_write_all as needed; read grants never imply write.
  • File mode only accesses app-authorized files. Explicitly select all mode for broader access and request drive_metadata_read, drive_read_all or drive_write_all only with user intent. Reuse the same shared account key to consent; read permission never implies write permission.

Retry and execution caution

  • File mode only accesses app-authorized files. Explicitly select all mode for broader access and request drive_metadata_read, drive_read_all or drive_write_all only with user intent. Reuse the same shared account key to consent; read permission never implies write permission.

How to verify the fix

  • The same intended account has explicit required access and the file is eligible in the selected mode.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials, content or resumable URLs.
  • Do not blindly repeat uncertain writes.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
